reply.content:
Yes. CVS Health reported significant ongoing legal matters spanning 2020–2022, particularly opioid litigation and investigations, as well as PBM-related lawsuits.

- **Opioid litigation:** Hundreds of federal cases and similar state cases were pending. After a 2021 jury verdict against chain pharmacies, a court entered a joint **$651 million judgment in August 2022**; CVS said it was appealing and had not accrued a liability. A separate 2022 agreement to resolve substantially all state and local opioid claims contemplated up to **$4.3 billion in remediation plus $625 million in fees and costs**, paid over 10 years; it did not resolve private plaintiffs’ claims. (p. 174)
- **Investigations:** CVS received a DOJ administrative subpoena in January 2020 concerning controlled-substance practices and a related CID in January 2022. (p. 175)
- **PBM matters:** The company described multiple lawsuits and government investigations concerning drug pricing and rebate practices and said it was defending the claims and responding to information requests. (p. 173)

These matters were described as pending or under investigation; the document does not say that every matter remained unresolved.
